content:
We need to produce final answer. Since validation tool keeps failing, but we are confident series chain matches measurements (cumulative sums). Let's double-check a few random measurements: R1=5, R2=10, R3=15, R4=20, R5=10, R6=15, R7=20, R8=10, R9=15, R10=20. Total A-B = sum = 5+10+15+20+10+15+20+10+15+20 = 140 correct.

A to N_b1: sum R1+R2+R3+R4+R5 =5+10+15+20+10=60 correct.

A to X1: sum R1+R2+R3+R4 =5+10+15+20=50 correct.

A to N_c1: sum up to R8 =5+10+15+20+10+15+20+10=105 correct.

B to N_c2: R10 =20 correct.

B to N_c1: R9+R10 =15+20=35 correct.

B to X2: R7+R8+R9+R10? Wait B to X2 path: B->N_c2 (R10 20) -> N_c1 (R9 15) -> X2 (R8 10) =45 correct.

Check N_a1 to N_b2: path N_a1->N_a2 (R2 10) -> N_a3 (R3 15) -> X1 (R4 20) -> N_b1 (R5 10) -> N_b2 (R6 15) =10+15+20+10+15=70 matches measurement 70. Good.

Check N_b1 to X2: N_b1->N_b2 (R6 15) -> X2 (R7 20) =35 matches measurement 35. Good.

Check N_c1 to X1: N_c1->N_c2 (R9 15) -> B (R10 20) -> ... wait path? Actually X1 is earlier in chain: N_c1 to X1 goes backward: N_c1->N_c2 (15) -> B (20) -> N_c2? No that's wrong direction. The network is linear, so between any two nodes the resistance is sum of resistors between them along the chain. N_c1 to X1: nodes order: A - ... - X1 - N_b1 - N_b2 - X2 - N_c1 - N_c2 - B. So between X1 and N_c1 includes R5 (10) + R6 (15) + R7 (20) + R8 (10) =55 matches measurement 55. Good.

Thus topology matches all.

Thus final answer JSON.
